column1: # check/spec/fnbody — user fn definitions and the body analysis pass.
# defq installs a fn from [input-sig, output-sig, body] triples
# (core.ParseFnDef / core.InstallFnDef, firing during the check pass via
# RunInCheck). Installing a boru-bodied fn is what drives the
# construction-time static body pass in check_fnbody.go and the
# AnalyseFnBody model in carrier.go: the body is analysed over carriers,
# its residual is conformance-checked against the declared output sig,
# and the result of a call site is the DECLARED return, not the body's
# residual.
# --- the body is analysed and the declared return commits at the call ---
defq incq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n 1 addq ] ] 5 incq
column3: declared Integer wins over the body's Number residual

column1: defq okq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Number ] [ n 1 addq ] ] 3 okq
defq add2q [ [ a:Integer b:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ a b addq ] ] 1 2 add2q
defq pfq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Boolean ] [ n predq ] ] 4 pfq
defq zeroq [ [ ] [ Integer ] [ 42 ] ] zeroq
defq tworq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer Integer ] [ n n ] ] 5 tworq
# --- an installed fn that is never called is diagnosed once ---
defq unusedq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n ] ]
# --- the body must CONFORM to the declaration ---
defq badq [ [ n:Integer ] [ String ] [ n 1 addq ] ] 1 badq
defq extraq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n n ] ] 5 extraq
column3: body leaves two values, declares one

column1: # --- a body word that resolves nowhere is caught inside the analysis ---
defq oopsq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n missingq ] ] 1 oopsq
# --- user-fn dispatch behaves like native dispatch at the call site ---
defq incq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n 1 addq ] ] "x" incq
defq polyq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n ] [ s:String ] [ String ] [ s ] ] 1 polyq
defq polyq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n ] [ s:String ] [ String ] [ s ] ] "a" polyq
# --- a literal in the input sig is a MATCH PATTERN, not a param name ---
defq patq [ [ 1 ] [ Integer ] [ 9 ] ] 1 patq
defq patq [ [ 1 ] [ Integer ] [ 9 ] ] 2 patq
column3: 2 does not match the literal pattern 1

column1: # --- a dynamic operand rides user-fn dispatch dynamically ---
defq incq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n 1 addq ] ] 1 anyq incq
# --- recursion is modelled without diverging (the analysis bails) ---
defq recq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n recq ] ] 1 recq
defq mutq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n mut2q ] ] defq mut2q [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n mutq ] ] 1 mutq
column3: mut2q's only caller is mutq's body; the pass still counts it unused

column1: # --- fns compose, redefine, and can be defined after other statements ---
defq aq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n 1 addq ] ] defq bq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n aq ] ] 2 bq
defq rdq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n ] ] defq rdq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n 1 addq ] ] 1 rdq
5 defq lateq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n ] ] lateq
# --- malformed specs refuse loudly ---
defq badlenq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] ]
# --- a body that nets NOTHING for a declared return always errors ---
defq noretq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ ] ] 5 noretq
column3: empty body, declared Integer: the call is a guaranteed program error

column1: defq nr2q [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ ] ] defq callq [ [ n:Integer ] [ Integer ] [ n nr2q ] ] 5 callq
column3: the same fault inside another fn's body is conditional, so silent
